thesis_he.bear: האשראי בברזיל מתקלקל (חובות בפיגור שיא, מס גבוה יותר על חברות פיננסיות, הגבלות שיווק אשראי מ-2027) ו-Mercado Pago מתחרה בחוזקה, כך שהיתרון בעלות לא מספיק כדי לשמור על תשואה של 30% על ההון.
thesis_he.base: נו שומרת על יתרון עלות ומימון זול מול איטאו ואינטר, ממשיכה לגדול בלקוחות ובהכנסה ללקוח, ומקסיקו מתחילה לתרום כבנק מלא, בזמן שהסיכון בברזיל (מטבע, מסים, אשראי) נשאר גבוה.
thesis_he.bull: מקסיקו כבנק מלא חוזרת על הדרך של ברזיל בשוק עם מעט אשראי, רישיון בנק בברזיל מאושר, ונו לוקחת עוד נתח מהבנקים הגדולים בלי שהפיגורים עולים.

market_direction.reading: Large, concentrated, still-growing pool: NU puts the retail revenue pool of Brazil, Mexico and Colombia at US$227.9B with NU about 5% of it, and banking concentration (HHI 889 Brazil, 993 Mexico vs 328 US). Mexico is under-penetrated (about 37% of adults with formal credit, 16% with a bank card) and management's illustrative gross-profit-pool CAGR is about 15% for Mexico vs about 8% for Brazil (not guidance). Direction in Brazil is mixed near term: household default on market-rate credit hit a record 8.09% in September 2026 (6.89% a year earlier) and Selic is still 13.75%.

bottleneck_potential.reading: NU is not a supply bottleneck: Pix and Open Finance are open public rails, so access is not scarce. What is scarce is cheap, well-underwritten funding and low cost to serve, where NU leads: deposits US$45.3B at 88% of the interbank rate (-3 pp y/y), cost to serve US$1.0 per active customer per month, efficiency 19.5%. Capacity is being added by rivals in the same unsecured consumer segment: Mercado Pago credit book +75% y/y (US$16B), Inter loans +29%.

share_trajectory.reading: NU is still taking share: customers 122.7M to 138.9M (+13% y/y), about 118M in Brazil (62% of adults at FY2025, customer growth above the five largest incumbents combined per BCB data in the 20-F); 2Q26 net income +49% vs Itau +7.8% and Inter +34%; Mexico revenue +54% in FY2025 (523.1 to 808.1M) and +79% y/y in 2Q26 (175.7 to 314.6M). The one named rival growing credit faster is Mercado Pago (book +75%, Mexico fintech MAU +45%).

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than Itau and Inter on returns, cost and engagement: ROE 33% vs Itau 24.3% vs Inter 16.3%; efficiency 19.5% vs Itau Brazil 35.5% vs Inter 42.1% (definitions differ); monthly activity 83.5% vs Inter 58.3% active clients. Weaker on credit quality: NPL 90+ 6.9% vs Itau 1.9% and Banorte 1.5%, a riskier low-income unsecured book. Against Mercado Pago NU is larger and more profitable but MELI grows its credit book faster and has the e-commerce data and distribution.

threats.reading: Regulation and tax: CSLL for certain financial companies rises to 17.5% from April 2026 and 20% from 2028 (Brazil is about 91% of revenue); BCB resolutions of 23 Oct 2026 limit unsolicited credit marketing from 2027 (a customer-acquisition and limit-increase lever); INSS payroll loans are rate-capped. Country risk: the 25 Oct 2026 election moved BRL about 10% intraday. Competition: Mercado Pago (+75% book) and Inter in the same segment; Open Finance and salary portability lower switching. Credit: record household default in Brazil.

moat.note: Cost and funding moat, evidenced against Itau (ROE 24.3%, Brazil efficiency 35.5%) and Inter (ROE 16.3%, efficiency 42.1%): NU earns ROE 33% at 19.5% efficiency with deposits at 88% of interbank and US$1.0 monthly cost to serve. ROIC is not computable for a bank (forensic roic unavailable); ROE ran 27-33% for seven quarters. Not access-based: Pix/Open Finance are open, and Mercado Pago is closing in on credit growth.

switching_costs.note: Pix, Open Finance and salary portability make switching easy in both directions; NU keeps customers through engagement and price, not lock-in.

retention.note: Monthly activity 83.5% held while customers grew 13% y/y; ARPAC US$12.5 to 17.1 (+22% FXN), so cohorts deepen rather than churn. Inter: 58.3% active.

pricing_power.note: NIM rose to 22.9% and risk-adjusted NIM to 12.4%, but management ties it to mix toward unsecured and higher-risk segments, not to price increases; payroll loans are rate-capped and incumbents compete on price.

customer_concentration.note: No customer is 10% of revenue (139M retail customers). Geographic concentration is the real concentration: Brazil 91% of revenue (see geopolitics).

market_size.note: NU puts its serviceable retail revenue pool at US$227.9B with about 5% share; Mexico under-penetrated, NU's Mexico gross-profit share under 1% of a US$43B pool (company analysis).

competition.note: Intense: Mercado Pago book +75% in Brazil and Mexico, Inter +29%, Itau and BBVA Mexico profitable incumbents. NU still grows fastest in net income and customers among the Brazil names.

substitutes.note: Open rails let any digital bank replicate the account and Pix (NU about 20% of Pix transfers, Inter about 9%); the substitute risk is other digital lenders, not a new technology.

management.note: Delivery is good: first US$1bn+ quarter, efficiency guided to about 20% for FY2026 and 19.5% in 2Q26, Mexico bank launched. Depth is the concern: new CFO Rob Livingston (from July 2026; change sourced from press) and CTO resignation effective 2026-11-12 with the founder-CEO interim. No numeric guidance track record (gap).

capital_allocation.note: US$500.4M of buybacks in 1H26 (avg about US$12.31) vs SBC US$216.8M, so net shrink; no dividend. But Brazil prudential CET1 fell 13.0% to 11.9% in six months (RWA +14.7%), and the US launch is a new cost centre with no revenue yet; Monzo talks denied.

governance.note: Founder David Velez holds about 74.4% of voting power through Class B shares; foreign private issuer (no Form 4). Managerial P&L since Q4'25 is reconciled to IFRS, but the 2Q26 IFRS tax rate of 14.2% (27.6% a year earlier) is not explained in what was read.

regulation.note: Net headwind in Brazil: CSLL to 17.5% then 20% from 2028, credit-marketing limits from 2027, payroll-rate caps, Brazil bank licence (Banco Porto Real) pending BCB approval. Positive: Mexico full bank licence live since August 2026.

technology_ai.note: NuFormer model in production on three credit portfolios, AI agents handle over 60% of Brazil support conversations, cost to serve US$1.0/month. CTO departure is a key-person watch item.

geopolitics.note: About 91% of revenue in BRL, reported in USD; the 25 Oct 2026 election moved BRL about 10% intraday and Brazilian equities sharply; fiscal deficits flagged by analysts. Diversification (Mexico 7%) is small.

gaps: Outside view (warning only, sets nothing): fast-growing consumer lenders in high-rate emerging markets historically see returns fade in credit downturns; NU's own credit data (NPL 90+ 6.9%, Stage 2 10.1% to 11.9%) is what counts.
ROIC / incremental ROIC unavailable for a bank (forensic screen); ROE used instead.
